links.reason: Mark says that from the beginning God “made them male and female”; Genesis says “male and female He created them.”
Mark repeats “a man will leave his father and mother” from Genesis, and ends with “one flesh.”
Mark says God “made them male and female”; Genesis says “Male and female He created them” and that He blessed them.
Mark has a voice from heaven say “You are My beloved Son”; Genesis has God say “your only son Isaac, whom you love.”
Mark has a voice from a cloud say “This is My beloved Son”; Genesis has God say “your only son Isaac, whom you love.”
Mark says a man is to “raise up offspring for him”; Genesis has Judah tell Onan to “raise up offspring for your brother.”
Mark says God told Moses, “I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac”; Exodus gives these words, and Moses hides his face.
Mark repeats “the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”; in Exodus, God says of it, “This is My name forever.”
Mark says Moses said “Honor your father and your mother”; Exodus has “Honor your father and mother,” with a promise of long days.
Mark lists “honor your father and mother” among the commandments; Exodus has the same words, then a promise of long days.
Mark lists “Do not murder” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not murder.”
Mark lists “do not commit adultery” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not commit adultery.”
Mark lists “do not steal” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not steal.”
Mark lists “do not bear false witness” among the commandments; Exodus adds “against your neighbor.”
Mark repeats “Anyone who curses his father or mother”; Exodus says such a person “must surely be put to death.”
Mark says “I will send My messenger ahead of You”; Exodus says “I am sending an angel before you.”
Mark repeats “Love your neighbor as yourself”; Leviticus has the same words, and ends “I am the LORD.”
Mark repeats “love your neighbor as yourself” within a saying that puts love above burnt offerings; Leviticus has the same words.
Mark says the crowd was “like sheep without a shepherd”; Numbers speaks of one who will lead the congregation so it is not like that.
Mark says “God is One and there is no other but Him”; Deuteronomy says “the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him.”
Mark says Moses said “Honor your father and your mother”; Deuteronomy has the same words.
In Mark, Jesus names the most important command by repeating Deuteronomy: “Hear, O Israel” and “The LORD our God, the LORD is One.”
Mark repeats Deuteronomy’s command to love God “with all your heart and with all your soul” and “with all your strength.”
Mark repeats Deuteronomy’s command to love God “with all your heart” and “with all your strength,” and adds love for the neighbor.
Mark has a voice from the cloud say, “Listen to Him!”; Deuteronomy says the LORD will raise up a prophet: “You must listen to him.”
Mark says Moses permitted a man “to write his wife a certificate of divorce”; Deuteronomy says he “may write her a certificate of divorce.”
Mark says Moses wrote that the man “is to marry his brother’s widow”; Deuteronomy says “Her husband’s brother is to take her as his wife.”
Mark says the crowd was “like sheep without a shepherd”; in 1 Kings Micaiah says Israel was scattered “like sheep without a shepherd.”
Mark has a voice from heaven say “You are My beloved Son”; Psalms says “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
Mark has a voice from the cloud say “This is My beloved Son”; Psalms says “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
Mark has Jesus cry out “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”, words that Psalms 22:1 also has.
Mark says they “divided His garments by casting lots”; Psalms says “They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.”
Mark says a sponge of “sour wine” was held up for Jesus to drink; Psalms 69:21 says “gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.”
Mark says David, speaking by the Holy Spirit, declared the words of Psalms: “Sit at My right hand”.
Mark has Jesus say the Son of Man will be “sitting at the right hand of Power”; Psalms says “Sit at My right hand”.
Mark says Jesus “sat down at the right hand of God”; Psalms says “Sit at My right hand”.
Mark repeats Psalms: “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone”.
Mark repeats Psalms: “This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes”.
Mark has the crowd shout “Hosanna!”; Psalms asks, “O LORD, save us, we pray”.
Mark says “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David”; Psalms says “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD”.
Mark has a man who “planted a vineyard”; Isaiah has a song: “My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill”.
Mark says the man “dug a wine vat” and “built a watchtower”; Isaiah says he “dug out a winepress” and “built a watchtower”.
Mark repeats Isaiah: “ever seeing but never perceiving” and “ever hearing but never understanding”.
Mark says “otherwise they might turn and be forgiven”; Isaiah says they might “turn and be healed”.
Mark repeats Isaiah: “honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me”.
Mark says “they teach as doctrine the precepts of men”; Isaiah says “Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men”.
Mark says “who will prepare Your way”; Isaiah says “Prepare the way for the LORD in the wilderness”.
Mark has a voice from heaven say “in You I am well pleased”; Isaiah says “My Chosen One, in whom My soul delights”.
Mark repeats Isaiah’s words “My house will be called a house of prayer” and “for all the nations.”
Mark repeats Isaiah’s words about “their worm” that never dies and a fire never “quenched.”
Mark repeats Jeremiah’s words about people who have “eyes” and “ears” but “do not see” and “do not hear.”
Mark repeats Jeremiah’s words “a den of robbers,” said of the house that Jeremiah says “bears My Name.”
Mark asks, “Having eyes, do you not see”; Ezekiel says a rebellious house has “eyes to see but do not see.”
Mark says the crowd was “like sheep without a shepherd”; Ezekiel says “They were scattered for lack of a shepherd.”
Mark repeats Daniel’s picture of “the Son of Man coming” with “the clouds.”
Mark repeats Daniel’s words “coming with the clouds of heaven” about the Son of Man.
Mark repeats “the abomination of desolation” from Daniel, standing where it should not be; Daniel says it is set up after the daily sacrifice stops.
Mark repeats “the abomination of desolation” from Daniel; Daniel gives “1,290 days” from the time the daily sacrifice is abolished.
Mark says the man “swings the sickle, because the harvest has come”; Joel says “Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe.”
Mark repeats Zechariah’s words “the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered,” with “I will strike” in Mark.
Mark and Malachi both have “Behold, I will send My messenger”; Mark says “ahead of You,” and Malachi says “before Me.”
Mark repeats Isaiah’s words “A voice of one calling” and “Prepare the way for the” Lord, with the voice in the wilderness.
Mark repeats Psalms: “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord”.
Mark repeats “with all your heart and with all your soul”; Deuteronomy 10:12 asks Israel to love and serve the LORD that way.
Mark repeats “with all your heart and with all your soul”; Deuteronomy says “you will love Him” that way, “so that you may live.”
Mark 9:44 has no words in the Berean Standard Bible; Isaiah says “their worm will never die, their fire will never be quenched.”
Mark 15:28 has no words in the Berean Standard Bible; Isaiah says “He was numbered with the transgressors.”
